entities.summary:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP — 'Indian People's Party') is India's current ruling party and the world's largest political party by membership with over 180 million members. Founded in 1980 from the remnants of the Janata Party, the BJP rose from 2 Lok Sabha seats in 1984 to win landslide victories in 2014 and 2019 under Narendra Modi, and won a reduced majority in the 2024 elections while remaining India's dominant party.

The BJP traces its ideological lineage to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a Hindu nationalist organization founded in 1925. The party's core ideology of Hindutva (Hindu nationalism) seeks to define India as a Hindu civilization-state, in contrast to the Indian National Congress's secular nationalism. The demolition of the Babri Masjid mosque in Ayodhya in 1992 — by Hindu nationalist mobs connected to BJP-aligned organizations — triggered communal riots killing 2,000 people and transformed Indian politics.

Narendra Modi's 2014 election victory with 282 seats ended a decade of Congress coalition rule, bringing Gujarat's development model to the national stage. The BJP-led government built 100 million toilets, connected 600,000 villages to roads, passed the Citizenship Amendment Act (2019) excluding Muslims from expedited citizenship, and opened the Ram Mandir temple at the Babri Masjid site in January 2024 — the culmination of Hindu nationalism's four-decade campaign.
